summary:
**Conversation Overview**

This conversation is a continuation of Matthew Lach's (M's) long-running computational audit project "The Method 1.6," specifically Phase R2 (a full read of every volume with no editing until the review closes). Claude operates in a strictly executorial role. The session began with Claude resuming mid-task from a compacted context, completing the final close steps of chat 74: writing HANDOFF-25.md, building BUILD101 compendia, and delivering outputs.

The substantive second half of the conversation was triggered by M raising a concern about session throughput — specifically that too much chat context was being consumed by the gate (the per-session verification sequence). Claude measured the problem from the chat 74 transcript: the gate consumed 32% of context, the close 10%, and three reading segments 57%. The two Drive bundle fetches alone left ~130 KB of unused base64 previews in context (13% of the chat). M ruled on four proposals: declined direct bundle uploads (storage constraints), and approved converting the gate and close into instruments (gate.py, close.py), moving rulings and deferred items into append-only bundle members (RULINGS-R2.md, DEFERRED.md), and implementing these changes immediately in chat 74 rather than waiting for chat 75.

Claude then built the full instrument suite: r2lib.py (shared library with functions lifted verbatim by AST from prior instruments, with two count-asserted parameterisations), gate.py (manifest verification against MANIFEST.tsv, golden-output diffing via banked NAME.out files, census, extent-sites, certificate — printing only mismatches), and close.py (guarded build with MANIFEST.tsv generation, append-only member support via --append, and reverse md5 recovery before writing). Fifteen golden outputs were banked for all deterministic instruments. The full instrument suite was tested including deliberate failure cases. The final build, BUILD101 (3,204,034 B, md5 893a9826a02ce6065715425d5603a796, 214 members), was delivered alongside HANDOFF-26 (10,675 B, down from HANDOFF-25's 21,875 B). The projected gate cost going forward is approximately 12% of a chat context (the Drive fetch previews remain per ruling 1), enabling an estimated four to five reading segments per chat instead of three.

**Tool Knowledge**

Google Drive bundle fetches via `search_files` with `title contains 'BUILD101_compendia' or title contains 'BUILD90_main'` and `pageSize 5, excludeContentSnippets` reliably locate the two live bundles. Each fetch result spills to `/mnt/user-data/tool_results/<id>.json` and must be decoded with `base64.b64decode(..., validate=True)` from the spill file — never from inline content, as each fetch leaves a ~65 KB base64 preview in context that is unused and costly. The two spill file paths must be noted after the fetch calls and substituted into the bootstrap script before running it. The bundle member extraction regex is `^<<<FILE: (.+?)>>>\n(.*?)<<<END FILE: \1>>>\n` with `re.S|re.M` flags, applied to the decoded bytes. Members of both bundles (main and compendia) are extracted into a single `/home/claude/members/` directory with no collisions expected; gate.py's `manifest` step then verifies every extracted file against both bundles via MANIFEST.tsv. Running `gate.py census` must precede any instrument run, as it refuses if `members/__pycache__` or a scratch `DEFECT-CENSUS.tsv` exists; `rm -rf members/__pycache__` is a required delete-only call before census and before any member census or build throughout the project.

== TEXT L2725–2757
2725 ### 12.11.0.4 The separation hypothesis, named
2726  Four families of result in this book hold *because the constraint graph is a tree*, and none of them
2727  says so. The factorising count, the recoverability of the order, the balance at a cut and the
2728  propagation of Chapter 15 all use it; §7.1 records treeness as a fact about Λ and never as a
2729  condition. **A hypothesis that is never stated cannot be checked, and the counterexample has been
2730  inside this book since the ninth axis.**
2731 
2732  **Λ₉′ is the test, and it separates the results.** Adding 2S′ ≤ 2f+1 closes the cycle f — g — 2S′ — f
2733  and buys 93 cells of tightness. Measured on both:
2734 
2735   property                                        Λ₉, a tree     Λ₉′, a cycle
2736   closure, E(X) = 0                               0              **0**
2737   factorisation over the transfer, defect         0              **0**
2738   conditional independence, f ⊥ 2S′ given g       0 of 16         **6 of 16**
2739 
2740  **Closure does not need the tree. Nor does the factorisation.** Both survive the cycle intact. What
2741  fails is conditional independence, and it fails at exactly one cut.
2742 
2743  **Which makes the hypothesis narrower than treeness, and this is the correction.** Remove q from
2744  either graph and the two ends fall apart — in Λ₉′ as much as in Λ₉ — because the cycle lies wholly on
2745  the target side and does not cross that cut. Remove g and in the tree f and 2S′ fall apart, while in
2746  Λ₉′ they stay joined by the new edge.
2747 
2748     **A result conditioned on a coordinate holds exactly when that coordinate separates the things
2749     being conditioned. Treeness is not the hypothesis; it is the condition under which the
2750     hypothesis holds at every cut at once.**
2751 
2752  In a tree every internal vertex is an articulation point, so the condition is free and nobody notices
2753  it is being used. Add one edge and it becomes a fact about *which* cut, which is why §12.11.5's
2754  factorisation survives Λ₉′ and §12.11.1's tightness costs what it costs. **The 93 cells are not paid
2755  for in generality across the board** — they are paid for at the cuts the new edge spans, and nowhere
2756  else. Register 347.
2757

input.file_text:
# r2-ch12i.py — Phase R2 instrument for main §12.11.0.4 "The separation hypothesis, named" (chat 74).
# Runs beside tower-2.py (imported by path). Λ₉ from tower-2.py; Λ₉′ = Λ₉ ∩ {2S′ ≤ 2f+1} (§12.11.1 L3096).
# Measures on every cell / every pair: closure, factorisation over the transfer q, the sixteen-cell test
# 2S′ ⊥ f | g (MC L1306), conditional independence against graph separation for all 252 (pair | coordinate)
# triples on both indices, and the two cut claims of L2743–2746.
import importlib.util, os, itertools
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import numpy as np
H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('tower2', os.path.join(H, 'tower-2.py'))
T = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(T)
NAMES = ['n', 'ℓ', 'k', 'q', 'e', 'f', 'g', '2S', '2S′']
SRC, TGT, Q = [0, 1, 2, 7], [4, 5, 6, 8], 3
EDGES9 = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (2, 7), (4, 5), (5, 6), (3, 6), (6, 8)]   # tower-2.py's bounds, one edge each
EDGES9P = EDGES9 + [(5, 8)]                                                  # + 2S′ ≤ 2f+1

def fmt(x): return f'{x:,}'

def closure(X):
    A = np.array(X, dtype=np.int64); n = len(A)
    rad = A.max(axis=0) + 1; w = np.cumprod(np.concatenate(([1], rad[:-1])))
    key = np.sort(A @ w)
    Ai, Aj = A[:, None, :], A[None, :, :]
    J = (np.maximum(Ai, Aj) @ w).ravel(); Mt = (np.minimum(Ai, Aj) @ w).ravel()
    jl = int((~np.isin(J, key)).sum()); ml = int((~np.isin(Mt, key)).sum())
    return n * n, jl, ml

def factor_q(X):
    A = defaultdict(set); B = defaultdict(set)
    for c in X:
        A[c[Q]].add(tuple(c[i] for i in SRC)); B[c[Q]].add(tuple(c[i] for i in TGT))
    return sum(len(A[v]) * len(B[v]) for v in A) - len(X)

def ci(X, a, b, c):
    """Exact (uniform-law) conditional independence a ⊥ b | c tested on every product cell (v, av, bv),
    av in the support of a given c=v, bv likewise: N(v,av,bv)·N(v) == N(v,av)·N(v,bv).
    Returns (product cells, cells failing the count test, cells with empty support)."""
    Nc, Na, Nb, Nab = Counter(), Counter(), Counter(), Counter()
    for x in X:
        Nc[x[c]] += 1; Na[(x[c], x[a])] += 1; Nb[(x[c], x[b])] += 1; Nab[(x[c], x[a], x[b])] += 1
    cells = fails = empty = 0
    for v in Nc:
        As = sorted(av for (vv, av) in Na if vv == v); Bs = sorted(bv for (vv, bv) in Nb if vv == v)
        for av in As:
            for bv in Bs:
                cells += 1
                if Nab[(v, av, bv)] * Nc[v] != Na[(v, av)] * Nb[(v, bv)]: fails += 1
                if Nab[(v, av, bv)] == 0: empty += 1
    return cells, fails, empty

def components(edges, removed, nodes=9):
    adj = defaultdict(set)
    for u, v in edges:
        if u not in removed and v not in removed: adj[u].add(v); adj[v].add(u)
    comp = {}
    for s in range(nodes):
        if s in removed or s in comp: continue
        stack = [s]; comp[s] = s
        while stack:
            u = stack.pop()
            for v in adj[u]:
                if v not in comp: comp[v] = s; stack.append(v)
    return comp

def separates(edges, c, a, b):
    comp = components(edges, {c}); return comp[a] != comp[b]

L9 = T.L9(); L9p = [c for c in L9 if c[8] <= 2 * c[5] + 1]
removed = sorted(set(L9) - set(L9p))
print(f'|Λ9| {fmt(len(L9))} | Λ9′ = Λ9 ∩ {{2S′ ≤ 2f+1}}: {fmt(len(L9p))} cells | removed {len(removed)} | '
      f'removed (f, g, 2S′) values {sorted(set((c[5], c[6], c[8]) for c in removed))} | '
      f'ambient box 27,648: fill Λ9 {len(L9)/27648:.2%}, Λ9′ {len(L9p)/27648:.2%}')
for name, X in (('Λ9 (tree)', L9), ('Λ9′ (cycle)', L9p)):
    pairs, jl, ml = closure(X)
    print(f'{name}: closure on {fmt(pairs)} pairs — join leaves {jl}, meet leaves {ml}, E(X) = {jl + ml} | '
          f'factorisation over q, Σ_q|A_q||B_q| − |X| = {factor_q(X)} | '
          f'2S′ ⊥ f | g on product cells (cells, count-test failures, empty-support cells) = {ci(X, 8, 5, 6)}')
# the g = 2 slice, both texts of the test
for name, X in (('Λ9', L9), ('Λ9′', L9p)):
    sl = Counter((x[5], x[8]) for x in X if x[6] == 2)
    Nf = Counter(x[5] for x in X if x[6] == 2); Ns = Counter(x[8] for x in X if x[6] == 2); N = sum(sl.values())
    print(f'   {name} g = 2 slice: N = {N}, N(f) = {dict(sorted(Nf.items()))}, N(2S′) = {dict(sorted(Ns.items()))}, '
          f'N(f,2S′) = {dict(sorted(sl.items()))}, exact-CI cells failing = '
          f'{sum(1 for f in Nf for s in Ns if sl[(f, s)] * N != Nf[f] * Ns[s])} of {len(Nf) * len(Ns)}')
cells_per_g = {v: (len({x[5] for x in L9 if x[6] == v}), len({x[8] for x in L9 if x[6] == v})) for v in range(4)}
print('   product cells per g (|F_g|, |S_g|):', cells_per_g, '| total', sum(a * b for a, b in cells_per_g.values()))
# conditional independence against separation, all 252 triples, both indices
res = {}
for name, X, E in (('Λ9', L9, EDGES9), ('Λ9′', L9p, EDGES9P)):
    tab = Counter(); out = {}
    for c in range(9):
        for a, b in itertools.combinations([i for i in range(9) if i != c], 2):
            sep = separates(E, c, a, b); cells, fails, empty = ci(X, a, b, c)
            holds = fails == 0; tab[(sep, holds)] += 1; out[(a, b, c)] = (sep, holds, fails, cells)
    res[name] = out
    sf = [(NAMES[a], NAMES[b], NAMES[c], f, n) for (a, b, c), (sep, holds, f, n) in out.items() if sep and not holds]
    nh = [(NAMES[a], NAMES[b], NAMES[c]) for (a, b, c), (sep, holds, f, n) in out.items() if (not sep) and holds]
    print(f'{name}: triples {sum(tab.values())} | separated & CI holds {tab[(True, True)]} | separated & CI fails {tab[(True, False)]} '
          f'| not separated & CI fails {tab[(False, False)]} | not separated & CI holds {tab[(False, True)]}')
    print(f'   separated-but-fails (Markov failures): {sf}')
    print(f'   not-separated-but-holds (counterexamples to "exactly when"): {nh}')
chg = [(NAMES[a], NAMES[b], NAMES[c], res['Λ9'][(a, b, c)][1], res['Λ9′'][(a, b, c)][1], res['Λ9′'][(a, b, c)][2], res['Λ9′'][(a, b, c)][3])
       for (a, b, c) in res['Λ9'] if res['Λ9'][(a, b, c)][1] != res['Λ9′'][(a, b, c)][1]]
print('CI verdict changes Λ9 → Λ9′ (a, b, c, holds9, holds9′, fails9′, cells):', chg, '| cuts involved:', sorted({t[2] for t in chg}))
sepchg = [(NAMES[a], NAMES[b], NAMES[c]) for c in range(9) for a, b in itertools.combinations([i for i in range(9) if i != c], 2)
          if separates(EDGES9, c, a, b) != separates(EDGES9P, c, a, b)]

display_content.code:
# r2-ch12i.py — Phase R2 instrument for main §12.11.0.4 "The separation hypothesis, named" (chat 74).
# Runs beside tower-2.py (imported by path). Λ₉ from tower-2.py; Λ₉′ = Λ₉ ∩ {2S′ ≤ 2f+1} (§12.11.1 L3096).
# Measures on every cell / every pair: closure, factorisation over the transfer q, the sixteen-cell test
# 2S′ ⊥ f | g (MC L1306), conditional independence against graph separation for all 252 (pair | coordinate)
# triples on both indices, and the two cut claims of L2743–2746.
import importlib.util, os, itertools
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import numpy as np
H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('tower2', os.path.join(H, 'tower-2.py'))
T = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(T)
NAMES = ['n', 'ℓ', 'k', 'q', 'e', 'f', 'g', '2S', '2S′']
SRC, TGT, Q = [0, 1, 2, 7], [4, 5, 6, 8], 3
EDGES9 = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (2, 7), (4, 5), (5, 6), (3, 6), (6, 8)]   # tower-2.py's bounds, one edge each
EDGES9P = EDGES9 + [(5, 8)]                                                  # + 2S′ ≤ 2f+1

def fmt(x): return f'{x:,}'

def closure(X):
    A = np.array(X, dtype=np.int64); n = len(A)
    rad = A.max(axis=0) + 1; w = np.cumprod(np.concatenate(([1], rad[:-1])))
    key = np.sort(A @ w)
    Ai, Aj = A[:, None, :], A[None, :, :]
    J = (np.maximum(Ai, Aj) @ w).ravel(); Mt = (np.minimum(Ai, Aj) @ w).ravel()
    jl = int((~np.isin(J, key)).sum()); ml = int((~np.isin(Mt, key)).sum())
    return n * n, jl, ml

def factor_q(X):
    A = defaultdict(set); B = defaultdict(set)
    for c in X:
        A[c[Q]].add(tuple(c[i] for i in SRC)); B[c[Q]].add(tuple(c[i] for i in TGT))
    return sum(len(A[v]) * len(B[v]) for v in A) - len(X)

def ci(X, a, b, c):
    """Exact (uniform-law) conditional independence a ⊥ b | c tested on every product cell (v, av, bv),
    av in the support of a given c=v, bv likewise: N(v,av,bv)·N(v) == N(v,av)·N(v,bv).
    Returns (product cells, cells failing the count test, cells with empty support)."""
    Nc, Na, Nb, Nab = Counter(), Counter(), Counter(), Counter()
    for x in X:
        Nc[x[c]] += 1; Na[(x[c], x[a])] += 1; Nb[(x[c], x[b])] += 1; Nab[(x[c], x[a], x[b])] += 1
    cells = fails = empty = 0
    for v in Nc:
        As = sorted(av for (vv, av) in Na if vv == v); Bs = sorted(bv for (vv, bv) in Nb if vv == v)
        for av in As:
            for bv in Bs:
                cells += 1
                if Nab[(v, av, bv)] * Nc[v] != Na[(v, av)] * Nb[(v, bv)]: fails += 1
                if Nab[(v, av, bv)] == 0: empty += 1
    return cells, fails, empty

def components(edges, removed, nodes=9):
    adj = defaultdict(set)
    for u, v in edges:
        if u not in removed and v not in removed: adj[u].add(v); adj[v].add(u)
    comp = {}
    for s in range(nodes):
        if s in removed or s in comp: continue
        stack = [s]; comp[s] = s
        while stack:
            u = stack.pop()
            for v in adj[u]:
                if v not in comp: comp[v] = s; stack.append(v)
    return comp

def separates(edges, c, a, b):
    comp = components(edges, {c}); return comp[a] != comp[b]

L9 = T.L9(); L9p = [c for c in L9 if c[8] <= 2 * c[5] + 1]
removed = sorted(set(L9) - set(L9p))
print(f'|Λ9| {fmt(len(L9))} | Λ9′ = Λ9 ∩ {{2S′ ≤ 2f+1}}: {fmt(len(L9p))} cells | removed {len(removed)} | '
      f'removed (f, g, 2S′) values {sorted(set((c[5], c[6], c[8]) for c in removed))} | '
      f'ambient box 27,648: fill Λ9 {len(L9)/27648:.2%}, Λ9′ {len(L9p)/27648:.2%}')
for name, X in (('Λ9 (tree)', L9), ('Λ9′ (cycle)', L9p)):
    pairs, jl, ml = closure(X)
    print(f'{name}: closure on {fmt(pairs)} pairs — join leaves {jl}, meet leaves {ml}, E(X) = {jl + ml} | '
          f'factorisation over q, Σ_q|A_q||B_q| − |X| = {factor_q(X)} | '
          f'2S′ ⊥ f | g on product cells (cells, count-test failures, empty-support cells) = {ci(X, 8, 5, 6)}')
# the g = 2 slice, both texts of the test
for name, X in (('Λ9', L9), ('Λ9′', L9p)):
    sl = Counter((x[5], x[8]) for x in X if x[6] == 2)
    Nf = Counter(x[5] for x in X if x[6] == 2); Ns = Counter(x[8] for x in X if x[6] == 2); N = sum(sl.values())
    print(f'   {name} g = 2 slice: N = {N}, N(f) = {dict(sorted(Nf.items()))}, N(2S′) = {dict(sorted(Ns.items()))}, '
          f'N(f,2S′) = {dict(sorted(sl.items()))}, exact-CI cells failing = '
          f'{sum(1 for f in Nf for s in Ns if sl[(f, s)] * N != Nf[f] * Ns[s])} of {len(Nf) * len(Ns)}')
cells_per_g = {v: (len({x[5] for x in L9 if x[6] == v}), len({x[8] for x in L9 if x[6] == v})) for v in range(4)}
print('   product cells per g (|F_g|, |S_g|):', cells_per_g, '| total', sum(a * b for a, b in cells_per_g.values()))
# conditional independence against separation, all 252 triples, both indices
res = {}
for name, X, E in (('Λ9', L9, EDGES9), ('Λ9′', L9p, EDGES9P)):
    tab = Counter(); out = {}
    for c in range(9):
        for a, b in itertools.combinations([i for i in range(9) if i != c], 2):
            sep = separates(E, c, a, b); cells, fails, empty = ci(X, a, b, c)
            holds = fails == 0; tab[(sep, holds)] += 1; out[(a, b, c)] = (sep, holds, fails, cells)
    res[name] = out
    sf = [(NAMES[a], NAMES[b], NAMES[c], f, n) for (a, b, c), (sep, holds, f, n) in out.items() if sep and not holds]
    nh = [(NAMES[a], NAMES[b], NAMES[c]) for (a, b, c), (sep, holds, f, n) in out.items() if (not sep) and holds]
    print(f'{name}: triples {sum(tab.values())} | separated & CI holds {tab[(True, True)]} | separated & CI fails {tab[(True, False)]} '
          f'| not separated & CI fails {tab[(False, False)]} | not separated & CI holds {tab[(False, True)]}')
    print(f'   separated-but-fails (Markov failures): {sf}')
    print(f'   not-separated-but-holds (counterexamples to "exactly when"): {nh}')
chg = [(NAMES[a], NAMES[b], NAMES[c], res['Λ9'][(a, b, c)][1], res['Λ9′'][(a, b, c)][1], res['Λ9′'][(a, b, c)][2], res['Λ9′'][(a, b, c)][3])
       for (a, b, c) in res['Λ9'] if res['Λ9'][(a, b, c)][1] != res['Λ9′'][(a, b, c)][1]]
print('CI verdict changes Λ9 → Λ9′ (a, b, c, holds9, holds9′, fails9′, cells):', chg, '| cuts involved:', sorted({t[2] for t in chg}))
sepchg = [(NAMES[a], NAMES[b], NAMES[c]) for c in range(9) for a, b in itertools.combinations([i for i in range(9) if i != c], 2)
          if separates(EDGES9, c, a, b) != separates(EDGES9P, c, a, b)]
print('separation changes Λ9 → Λ9′ (graph only):', sepchg)
# the cut claims of L2743–2746
for name, E in (('Λ9', EDGES9), ('Λ9′', EDGES9P)):
    cq = components(E, {Q}); cg = components(E, {6})
    print(f'{name}: remove q → source {{n,ℓ,k,2S}} one component {len({cq[i] for i in SRC}) == 1}, target {{e,f,g,2S′}} one component {len({cq[i] for i in TGT}) == 1}, '
          f'source and target separated {len({cq[i] for i in SRC} | {cq[i] for i in TGT}) == 2} | remove g → f and 2S′ joined {cg[5] == cg[8]}')
tree_art = [NAMES[v] for v in range(9) if len(set(components(EDGES9, {v}).values())) > 1]
print('Λ9 tree articulation points:', tree_art, '| leaves:', [NAMES[v] for v in range(9) if sum(v in e for e in EDGES9) == 1])

# READ-ch12i — Phase R2, main volume §12.11.0.4 "The separation hypothesis, named" (chat 74)

Member The_Method_1_6-2.md (BUILD90 main, md5 4aef772b…), L2725–L2757 (33 lines, none over 400 characters; §12.11.0.5 opens at L2758), read in full against each cited section (§7.1 L1750–1763, §7.2 L1764–1775, §8.5 L1901, §10.4 L2060, §12.11.1 L3032 with L3096–3097, §12.11.5 L3462, Chapter 15 L4270–4331), the Register (347), the Mathematical Compendium (L1306, L1726–1728), the rebuilt tower (tower-2.py, c0bce27a…), the segment instrument r2-ch12i.py (beside tower-2.py; Λ₉ and Λ₉′ = Λ₉ ∩ {2S′ ≤ 2f+1} rebuilt, closure on every pair of each, the factorisation over q, the sixteen-cell test, exact conditional independence against graph separation on all 252 (pair | coordinate) triples of each index, the two cut claims) and r2-tools.py. Rulings applied as in READ-ch7. Census rows in range: 1062 (defect), 1063 (not a defect) — CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch12i.tsv.

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**12i-01 · L2728 — "§7.1 records treeness" points to a section that does not mention it.** PRINTED L2728: `propagation of Chapter 15 all use it; §7.1 records treeness as a fact about Λ and never as a`. SOURCE: §7.1 "The constraints, and where each comes from" is L1750–1763 and contains no 'tree' (grep); the statement is §7.2 "Every constraint is of one form", L1769 `**Consequence, developed in Chapter 8:** the graph whose nodes are coordinates and whose edges are constraints is a **tree**.` and L1773–1774 `Eight nodes, seven edges, connected — a tree, and therefore treewidth 1. Three results in this book follow from that fact alone.`, developed at §8.5 "The constraint graph is a tree" (L1901). The same mis-pointer stands at §18.4.1 L5150 (`Λ's own shape, which §7.1 says three central results follow from`) — for the Chapter 18 segment. Pointer, lower. For R3: "§7.2" (or "§8.5").

**12i-02 · L2726–2729 — "none of them says so" and "never as a condition" are stale as printed.** PRINTED L2726–2729: `Four families of result in this book hold *because the constraint graph is a tree*, and none of them says so. The factorising count, the recoverability of the order, the balance at a cut and the propagation of Chapter 15 all use it; §7.1 records treeness as a fact about Λ and never as a condition.` SOURCE, as printed in BUILD90: §7.2 L1774 `Three results in this book follow from that fact alone.`; §8.5 L1908 `A tree has no cycles, so there is nothing for inclusion–exclusion to correct.` and L1910 `Chapter 15 recovers Λ's coordinate orders from an unlabelled bag of cells by propagation along this tree — 20 of 20.`; §10.4 L2061 `Because the constraint graph is a tree, the count factorises:`; §15.4 L4308–4309 `propagation along the tree / If the constraint graph is a tree, each axis is constrained only by its parent.` and L4327 `a tree. For an index whose graph has cycles, S2 is open`; §12.11.5 L3466 `every coupling axis hangs off one side of the tree`; §30.1 L8322 `Chapter 15 recovers Λ's coordinate order because its constraint graph is a tree.`; D.4.4.3 L10459 `the reason §11.7's proof has a hypothesis — the tree`. Three of the four families state the condition in their own sections (the count, the propagation, the factorisation), and §15.4 states it as a hypothesis (`If the constraint graph is a tree`). Also L2726 `Four families` against §7.2 L1774 and §18.4.1 L5150 `Three results` — the count is not reconciled anywhere. Stale self-description (the section reads as written at Register 347, before the later statements), lower; noted per M's priorities. The section's substance — the hypothesis is narrower than treeness — is measured true (B).

**12i-03 · layout.** L2735–2738 column-dump table; L2748–2750 four-space paragraph renders as code. Production.

## B. Verified (all MEASURED unless marked; r2-ch12i.py)

- L2732–2733 Λ₉′ = Λ₉ ∩ {2S′ ≤ 2f+1}: 1,654 − 93 = 1,561 cells; the 93 removed cells are exactly (f, g, 2S′) = (0, 2, 2) — §12.11.1 L3097 verbatim `The 93 cells it cuts are exactly (f = 0, g = 2, 2S′ = 2)`; MC L1726 `Λ₉′ = 1,561 cells, 93 removed; closes the cycle f–g–2S′`; the tower row L2938 (1,561 of 27,648 = 5.65 %) reproduces. The new bound is one edge f–2S′ on the nine-node graph, which closes f — g — 2S′ — f (g–2S′ from 2S′ ≤ g, f–g from g ≤ 4f+2).
- L2736 closure: E(X) = 0 on both — join and meet leave the set on 0 of 2,735,716 ordered pairs of Λ₉ and 0 of 2,436,721 of Λ₉′.
- L2737 factorisation over the transfer: Σ_q |A_q(X)|·|B_q(X)| − |X| = 0 on both (A = (n, ℓ, k, 2S), B = (e, f, g, 2S′) projections per q-fibre).
- L2738 `conditional independence, f ⊥ 2S′ given g  0 of 16  6 of 16`: reproduces under the test MC L1306 names (`2S′ ⊥ f | g over its sixteen cells, six failing on Λ₉′ and none on the tree`) read as exact conditional independence of the uniform law, N(g, f, 2S′)·N(g) = N(g, f)·N(g, 2S′), on the sixteen product cells Σ_g |F_g|·|S_g| = 2 + 4 + 6 + 4 (g = 0, 1, 2, 3). Λ₉: 0 of 16. Λ₉′: 6 of 16 — all six cells of the g = 2 slice (N = 372; N(f) = {0: 186, 1: 186}; N(2S′) = {0: 155, 1: 155, 2: 62}; N(f, 2S′) = {(0,0) 93, (0,1) 93, (0,2) 0, (1,0) 62, (1,1) 62, (1,2) 62}, against Λ₉'s slice N = 465 with (0,2) = 93). The support (product-set) test gives 1 of 16 — the emptied cell — so the printed six is the exact-law test, the notion Theorem 12.11.0.7 (L2819–2825) uses. Main L2836 `6 violations of 16` is the same figure.
- L2740–2741 `it fails at exactly one cut`: over all 252 triples, the conditional-independence verdict changes from Λ₉ to Λ₉′ at exactly two triples, both conditioned on g — (f, 2S′ | g) 6 of 16 and (e, 2S′ | g) 9 of 26 — and the graph's separation verdict changes at exactly the same two. One cut, g.
- L2743–2746 the cut claims: removing q leaves {n, ℓ, k, 2S} connected, {e, f, g, 2S′} connected and the two apart, in Λ₉ and in Λ₉′ alike (the new edge lies on the target side); removing g parts f from 2S′ in Λ₉ and leaves them joined in Λ₉′.
- L2748–2750 `holds exactly when that coordinate separates`: on all 252 (pair | coordinate) triples of Λ₉ — separated & independent 64, separated & dependent 0, not separated & dependent 188, not separated & independent 0 — and of Λ₉′ — 62 · 0 · 190 · 0 — exact conditional independence holds if and only if the coordinate separates the pair in the constraint graph. Both directions survive on the full population (the ⇐ direction is the global Markov property of an index cut out by one bound per edge; the ⇒ direction holds here because no edge bound is vacuous in any fibre — INFERRED as the reason, MEASURED as the fact).
- L2752 `In a tree every internal vertex is an articulation point`: Λ₉'s articulation points are ℓ, k, q, f, g — every non-leaf (leaves n, e, 2S, 2S′).
- L2753–2754 pointers: §12.11.5 (L3462) carries the factorisation over the transfer at L3463 (`Every stage of the tower factorises exactly over the transfer`); §12.11.1 (L3032) carries the tightness and its 93 cells at L3096–3097. Chapter 15 (L4270) resolves; its propagation is §15.4 L4308.
- L2756 Register 347 (R L1271–1274) resolves — `TREENESS WAS LOAD-BEARING IN FOUR FAMILIES OF RESULT AND NEVER STATED AS A HYPOTHESIS … a result conditioned on a coordinate holds exactly when that coordinate separates.` — the section's finding, without figures.
- Census 1063 (C9 "never", L2729 `A hypothesis that is never stated cannot be checked`): a general maxim, not a claim about a site — not a defect.

## C. Incidental

- The section names one failing pair; on Λ₉′ two pairs lose independence at g — f ⊥ 2S′ (6 of 16) and e ⊥ 2S′ (9 of 26) — because the new edge f–2S′ also gives e a path to 2S′ that avoids g. The cut count ("exactly one") is unaffected.
- "16" is defined nowhere in the main; MC L1306 defines it (the sixteen product cells). A reader of the main has the number without its unit.
- §12.11.0.5 L2779 calls propagation `the fourth independent result to break at Λ₉′` and §12.11.0.7 L2838 calls the Markov property `the third` — the reader meets "fourth" before "third"; record in those segments.
- "the balance at a cut" (L2727) is not a section title anywhere; INFERRED to mean §12.11.5's factorisation over the transfer (L3463) — settle in the §12.11.5 segment (G0v).
- r2-ch12i.py's `ci(X, a, b, c)` (exact and support tests on every product cell), `separates()` and `closure()` (numpy, every pair) are reusable for any coordinate triple or subset of a Λ₉-sized index.

2758 ### 12.11.0.5 What the cycle costs propagation — Q item O, closed
2759  §12.11.0.4 shows the separation hypothesis failing at Λ₉′. **Chapter 15's order recovery by tree
2760  propagation fails there too, and the failure is measurable.** Appendix E carried this as item O,
2761  *buildable, days*; it is one computation.
2762 
2763  **In a tree there is one path between any two coordinates, so a bound recovered by propagating along
2764  it is the bound.** With a cycle there are two, and they need not agree. Recovering the bound on 2S′
2765  from f, directly and by composing through g:
2766 
2767   index                     direct φ̂(2S′ | f)     composed through g     verdict
2768   Λ₉, a tree                {0: 2, 1: 3}          {0: 2, 1: 3}           **agree**
2769   Λ₉′, a cycle              **{0: 1, 1: 3}**      {0: 2, 1: 3}           **disagree at f = 0**
2770 
2771  **The direct edge is strictly tighter.** Composing along the tree path gives 2 where the constraint
2772  gives 1, so **propagation overstates the bound** — it does not fail loudly, it returns a weaker answer
2773  that looks like an answer.
2774 
2775     **A tree makes propagation sound by making it path-independent. A cycle does not make it wrong;
2776     it makes it lossy, and the loss is silent.**
2777 
2778  And the failure is **directional**: recovering f from 2S′ agrees in both objects. Only the direction
2779  the new edge tightens is affected. **This is the fourth independent result to break at Λ₉′**, with the
2780  cut law, the two-parent count and the Markov property — and it is the one that explains the others,
2781  since each of those is a propagation argument wearing different clothes. Register 364.
2782

2784  Before φ̂ was defined, the eleventh axis carried the bound **2J_c ≤ k**, and whether it contains the
2785  physical region was left open as item K, *retrievable, hours*. It is one enumeration, and the answer
2786  is no.
2787 
2788   occupancy k    largest physical 2J_c    2J_c ≤ k admits    φ̂(k) admits
2789   1                                  3                  1              **3**
2790   2                                  4                  2              **4**
2791   3                                  5                  3              **5**
2792 
2793  **The earlier bound excludes physical states at every occupancy**, not at some. A term of a p² shell
2794  can reach 2J_c = 4 where k = 2 permits 2. So 2J_c ≤ k was not a loose bound that happened to hold; it
2795  was the wrong bound, and had it survived, the index would have refused states the physics produces.
2796 
2797  **And φ̂ contains the physical region exactly** — it equals the realised maxima at every k, neither
2798  admitting a state that cannot occur nor excluding one that can. That is why §12.11.3.1 records it as a
2799  bound taken from the **extent** rather than from a law: it is the tightest containing bound and it was
2800  read off the object rather than derived. **The exactness is the reason it cannot be exact** — a bound
2801  that fits its own extent perfectly has no independent authority, which is what the third value of the
2802  provenance column names. Register 365.

# READ-ch12j — Phase R2, main volume §12.11.0.5 "What the cycle costs propagation — Q item O, closed" and §12.11.0.6 "The earlier bound on the core, tested — Q item K, closed" (chat 74)

Member The_Method_1_6-2.md (BUILD90 main, md5 4aef772b…), L2758–L2803 (46 lines, none over 400 characters; §12.11.0.7 opens at L2804), read in full against each cited section (§12.11.0.4 L2725, Chapter 15 L4270 with §15.4 L4308, §12.11.3.1 L3409–3461, Appendix E L10898–11010), the Register (364, 365), the rebuilt tower (tower-2.py, c0bce27a…), the segment instrument r2-ch12j.py (beside tower-2.py; propagated bounds φ̂(b | a) direct and composed through an intermediate on every cell of Λ₉ and Λ₉′, for the printed pair in both directions and for every (ordered pair, separator) composition of each index; the largest physical 2J_c at each occupancy enumerated from the antisymmetric microstates of s and p shells; φ̂ and 2J_c ≤ k; the provenance column of §12.11.3.1) and r2-tools.py. Rulings applied as in READ-ch7. Census rows in range: none (CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch12j.tsv is the header).

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**12j-01 · L2800–2802 — "the third value of the provenance column" is not extent.** PRINTED L2800–2802: `**The exactness is the reason it cannot be exact** — a bound that fits its own extent perfectly has no independent authority, which is what the third value of the provenance column names. Register 365.` SOURCE §12.11.3.1: the column's values in row order are law (D1–10, 13), **extent** (D11, 2J_c, L3424) and weakened (D12, K, L3425), and the section names its third value itself — L3428–3429 `**The provenance column has three values, not two**, and the third is where the tower spends its exactness.` and L3431 `**Dimension 12 is the third kind, and it is the one the book chose.**` … L3435 `**The law is not abandoned but weakened**`. The value that names an extent-bound's want of authority is *extent*, the second; the third is *weakened*. Register 365 (R L1357) says only `§12.11.3.1 files it under extent rather than law`. Cross-reference, lower. For R3: "which is what the provenance column's *extent* names".

**12j-02 · L2785 — "item K, retrievable, hours" has no site.** PRINTED L2784–2785: `whether it contains the physical region was left open as item K, *retrievable, hours*.` SOURCE: Appendix E's row L10954 `K  the earlier bound 2J_c ≤ k, tested for containment  CLOSED  —  —  mathematical` prints no obstacle or cost; Register 365 does not carry the earlier classification; no other line of the main or the Register carries "retrievable, hours" for K (grep). Item O's prior classification is carried — Register 364 R L1353 `where the book had listed it as buildable, days`. Provenance, lower; class of 12h-02.

**12j-03 · layout.** L2767–2769 and L2788–2791 column-dump tables; L2775–2776 four-space paragraph renders as code. Production.

## B. Verified (all MEASURED unless marked; r2-ch12j.py)

- L2759 §12.11.0.4 (L2725) resolves to the separation finding (READ-ch12i); L2759–2760 Chapter 15's tree propagation is §15.4 L4308–4309 `propagation along the tree / If the constraint graph is a tree, each axis is constrained only by its parent`; L2760 Appendix E (L10898) row O L10957 `tree propagation retested on Λ₉′'s f–g–2S′ cycle  CLOSED`, and L10969 `item O closed, item K closed`.
- L2763–2764 `a bound recovered by propagating along it is the bound`: on Λ₉, for every ordered pair (a → b) and every coordinate c that separates a from b, the direct bound φ̂(b | a) equals the bound composed through c — 128 of 128 compositions; on Λ₉′ likewise for the separators of its own graph, 124 of 124. Composition through a coordinate that does not separate disagrees freely on both (134 and 136 of those compositions), which is the sense of "the path".
- L2767–2769 the table: Λ₉ direct φ̂(2S′ | f) = {0: 2, 1: 3}, composed through g {0: 2, 1: 3}, agree; Λ₉′ direct {0: 1, 1: 3}, composed through g {0: 2, 1: 3}, disagree at f = 0 — g no longer separates f from 2S′ (r2-ch12i). Register 364 (R L1353) carries the same figures.
- L2771–2773 the direct edge is tighter (1 against 2 at f = 0), so composition overstates the bound; L2778 `recovering f from 2S′ agrees in both objects`: direct φ̂(f | 2S′) = {0: 1, 1: 1, 2: 1, 3: 1} = composed through g, on Λ₉ and on Λ₉′.
- L2779–2781 the three companions named — the cut law (§12.11.5 L3476), the two-parent count (§12.11.3.1 L3433–3435, §A.15, register 230) and the Markov property (§12.11.0.7 L2836) — each resolves to a section; Register 364 (R L1351–1354) resolves and matches the section.
- L2784 the eleventh axis is 2J_c (§12.11.3.1 row D11 L3424; tower-2.py index 10); L2785 Appendix E row K L10954 CLOSED.
- L2788–2791 the table: largest physical 2J_c by occupancy, enumerated as the largest 2·M_J over antisymmetric microstates of the s and p shells (ℓ ≤ 1 under §7.4's caps) = {1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5}; 2J_c ≤ k admits 1, 2, 3; φ̂ = {1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5} (tower-2.py PHI; minmax.py's "φ̂ … realised" agree). Excluded at every occupancy: 3 > 1, 4 > 2, 5 > 3.
- L2793–2794 a p² shell reaches 2J = 4 (³P₂ / ¹D₂; microstate maximum 4) where k = 2 permits 2.
- L2797–2799 φ̂ equals the physical maxima at every k (above), which is the containment claim; §12.11.3.1 L3439–3441 says the same (`φ̂ = {1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5}, and the largest 2J actually realised at each occupancy is {1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5}`) and files the bound under extent at L3424. Register 365 (R L1355–1358) resolves and matches.

## C. Incidental

- "Directional" holds for the book's φ̂ (upper bounds — §7.2's one form). Read as the lower bound the same edge implies on f, min f | 2S′ is 1 at 2S′ = 2 directly and 0 composed through g on Λ₉′ (Λ₉: agree) — the reverse direction also loses under lower-bound recovery.
- On the cycle the two paths from e to 2S′ differ: through f, φ̂(2S′ | e) = {1: 1, 2: 3, 3: 3} = direct; through g, {1: 2, 2: 3, 3: 3}. The tight path is the direct edge's.
- "Realised maxima" on the rebuilt tower are φ̂ by construction (tower-2.py's L11 draws 2J_c from range(φ̂(k) + 1)); the realised maxima of the original construction are record-carried (§12.11.3.1 L3439–3440, Register 365). The independent content measured here is φ̂ = the physical maxima.
- §12.11.0.5 L2779 `fourth independent result to break at Λ₉′` precedes §12.11.0.7 L2838 `the third` in reading order (READ-ch12i C).
- Appendix E's L10989 `Eleven items: one nonexistent, two buildable, eight retrievable` is for the Appendix E segment (with 12d-01's owed item and L8794/L11107).
- r2-ch12j.py's `direct()` / `composed()` (any aggregate) and its microstate enumeration are reusable for any propagated bound or shell maximum.

input.file_text:
# r2-ch12k.py — Phase R2 instrument for main §12.11.0.7 "Why the arrows agree — a decay theorem" (chat 74).
# Runs beside tower-2.py (imported by path). The (g, G) index as r2-ch12g.py builds it: Λ₈ × {g ≤ G ≤ 4f+2} × {0 ≤ 2S′ ≤ G},
# 13,775 cells, coordinates (n, ℓ, k, q, e, f, g, 2S, G, 2S′). Arrows per §12.11.0.2 L2660, A_w = {w(tgt) ≤ w(src)}:
# shell e ≤ n, subshell f ≤ ℓ, occupancy G ≤ k, spin 2S′ ≤ 2S. Measured on every cell: the six overlaps
# P(A∩B)/P(A)P(B), the mutual informations under three readings (arrow indicators; source coordinates; (src, tgt) pairs),
# the Pinsker bound, the constraint graph, and the conditional independences the chain argument uses.
import importlib.util, os, itertools, math
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('tower2', os.path.join(H, 'tower-2.py')); T = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(T)
n_, l_, k_, q_, e_, f_, g_, S_, G_, Sp_ = range(10)
NAMES = ['n', 'ℓ', 'k', 'q', 'e', 'f', 'g', '2S', 'G', '2S′']
X = [c + (G, S2p) for c in T.L8() for G in range(c[g_], 4 * c[f_] + 2 + 1) for S2p in range(0, G + 1)]
N = len(X)
ARROWS = {'shell': (n_, e_), 'subshell': (l_, f_), 'occupancy': (k_, G_), 'spin': (S_, Sp_)}   # (source coord, target coord)
ind = {w: [1 if c[t] <= c[sc] else 0 for c in X] for w, (sc, t) in ARROWS.items()}
DIST = {('shell', 'subshell'): 1, ('subshell', 'occupancy'): 1, ('occupancy', 'spin'): 1, ('subshell', 'spin'): 2, ('shell', 'occupancy'): 2, ('shell', 'spin'): 3}

def mi(xs, ys):
    cx, cy, cxy = Counter(xs), Counter(ys), Counter(zip(xs, ys))
    return sum(v / N * math.log2(v * N / (cx[x] * cy[y])) for (x, y), v in cxy.items())

print(f'(g, G) index: {N:,} cells | arrows |A_w|: ' + ', '.join(f'{w} {sum(v):,}' for w, v in ind.items()))
print('pair                    d   overlap P(A∩B)/P(A)P(B)   |P(A∩B)−P(A)P(B)|   I(A_u;A_v) bits   Pinsker √(I ln2/2)   I(u;v) source coords   I((u,u′);(v,v′))')
rows = []
for (u, v), d in DIST.items():
    pa, pb = sum(ind[u]) / N, sum(ind[v]) / N; pab = sum(a & b for a, b in zip(ind[u], ind[v])) / N
    ov = pab / (pa * pb); dev = abs(pab - pa * pb); iab = mi(ind[u], ind[v]); pins = math.sqrt(iab * math.log(2) / 2)
    su, sv = ARROWS[u][0], ARROWS[v][0]
    icoord = mi([c[su] for c in X], [c[sv] for c in X])
    ipair = mi([(c[ARROWS[u][0]], c[ARROWS[u][1]]) for c in X], [(c[ARROWS[v][0]], c[ARROWS[v][1]]) for c in X])

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**12k-01 · L2823–2824 with L2827 — the Pinsker step bounds the arrows by the wrong mutual information.** PRINTED L2820–2824: `let A_u, A_v be the arrows of coordinates u and v at tree distance d … **(ii)** hence by the data-processing inequality I(u;v) is non-increasing in d; **(iii)** hence by Pinsker, |P(A_u ∩ A_v) − P(A_u)·P(A_v)| ≤ √( I(u;v)·ln2 / 2 ).` and L2827–2828 `Mutual information, recomputed: **0.353 · 0.227 · 0.199** at d = 1, **0.094 · 0.070** at d = 2, **0.020** at d = 3 — strictly decreasing, as the theorem requires.` MEASURED: the recomputed figures are the mutual informations of the source coordinates alone — I(ℓ;k) 0.353, I(k;2S) 0.227, I(n;ℓ) 0.199, I(n;k) 0.094, I(ℓ;2S) 0.070, I(n;2S) 0.020 (bits, on 13,775 cells). Also the recomputed figures are listed in descending order, not in the table's row order, and the pairing is nowhere stated: the table's first row (occupancy ∩ spin, 1.466) has the second mutual information (0.227), and the largest, 0.353, belongs to subshell ∩ occupancy. Class of 12f-02 (figures right, label wrong); proof step, lower. For R3: state the theorem on the pairs (u, u′) and print the six mutual informations against their pairs.

**12k-02 · L2819 — the hypothesis "constraint graph is a tree" is not satisfied by the index the section measures.** PRINTED L2819: `**Theorem.** Let X be an index whose constraint graph is a tree`. SOURCE: the overlaps and mutual informations are measured on the (g, G) extended index (MC L1306; §12.11.0.2 L2645 `under g ≤ G ≤ 2(2f+1) and g ≤ q`), whose constraint graph has ten nodes and ten edges — G is bounded by g below and by f above while f–g is already an edge — the cycle f–g–G–f. ## C. Incidental

- Within d = 1 the overlap order (occupancy ∩ spin > subshell ∩ occupancy > shell ∩ subshell) is not the mutual-information order (I(ℓ;k) > I(k;2S) > I(n;ℓ)); the two rankings agree across classes, not within them — which is what L2830–2832's "the bound is loose" concedes.

Measured from chat 74's transcript (byte shares of the whole chat):

- Gate 32 %, close 10 %, the three reading segments 57 % (26 / 17 / 14 — each cheaper than the last as the reusable code accumulated).
- Inside the gate, the two Drive fetches are the largest single item: each left a ~65 KB base64 preview in context (65,351 and 65,345 characters — the main bundle's head, the compendia's middle), 13 % of the whole chat, and useless, since both bundles are decoded from the spilled files. The rest of the gate is by-eye comparison of ~60 member md5s and ~150 lines of instrument output against a handoff that is now 22 KB and grows ~2.5 KB a chat (INFERRED for the by-eye share).

Proposal:

1. The bundles arrive by direct upload, not Drive fetch: one archive (`METHOD-PACK-BUILDnnn.tar.gz` holding BUILD90 main and the current compendia bundle) attached to the opening prompt beside HANDOFF-NN.md. An archive upload puts only a path in context; the md5 check is unchanged, so authentication is unchanged. Drive stays the store — the same pack is uploaded to Materials at close. Fallback if no pack is attached: fetch by title as now. (Never attach a .md bundle directly — a markdown upload lands in context whole.) This amends the chat-68 gate ruling.
2. Instruments (my design): `gate.py` — verifies bundle bytes/md5/lines, extracts members, checks every member against a `MANIFEST.tsv` member written at build time, runs tower/kinds/minmax/census/r2-tools and the prior chat's instruments against banked golden outputs (`r2-chNN.out` members), prints only mismatches and PASS/FAIL; `close.py` — appends W-NNN and the members, measures, diffs, reverses, regenerates the manifest, writes the pack; `r2lib.py` — the shared functions now scattered across r2-ch12c…k.
3. Handoff form: identity (chat, build, Register range, md5s), next work, Drive actions, prompt — about 6 KB. The rulings list and the deferred list move to append-only members (`RULINGS-R2.md`, `DEFERRED.md`), so the handoff stops growing.
4. Timing: either now, in this chat (compaction has freed context — INFERRED; the work is file-grounded, BUILD100 and all members are on disk), producing BUILD101 + pack + HANDOFF-26 and retiring HANDOFF-25/BUILD100 unused; or as chat 75's first segment.

Projection (INFERRED): gate 32 → ~6 %, close 10 → ~5 %, so about five reading segments a chat instead of three.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""gate.py — the §0 gate as an instrument (chat 74, ruling 2). Every step must be able to fail.
Steps (each its own tool call, `timeout 280`):
  manifest [--main PATH] [--comp PATH]   verify every member of BOTH bundles against MANIFEST.tsv (bytes, md5, lines),
                                         and every extracted file in members/ against the bundle text
  run NAME...  | run --core | run --all  run instruments and diff stdout against the banked NAME.out (prints only mismatches)
  census                                 run census.py, compare /home/claude/DEFECT-CENSUS.tsv to the member byte for byte
  extent-sites                           print the "1 to N" / "1 to N-1" sites of the six reader-facing volumes (N from Register L6)
  bank NAME...                           run and write NAME.out (refuses to overwrite) — used at close for new instruments
  cert CHAT                              write /home/claude/GATE-chCHAT.txt from the log; PASS only if every step passed
Commands: NAME.out ↔ `python3 NAME.py` in members/, except SPECIAL below. Log: /home/claude/gate-log.tsv (append-only)."""
import sys, os, re, hashlib, subprocess, time, difflib
H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))            # /home/claude/members
HOME = os.path.dirname(H)                                 # /home/claude
MAIN = os.path.join(HOME, 'The_Method_1_6_BUILD90_main_and_register.md')
LOG = os.path.join(HOME, 'gate-log.tsv')
VOLS = ['The_Method_1_6-2.md', 'The_Method_1_6___The_Register-2.md', 'The_Method_1_6___Mathematical_Compendium-2.md',
        'The_Method_1_6___The_Physics_Compendium-2.md', 'The_Method_1_6___The_Index_of_Indices-2.md', 'The_Method_1_6___Spectra_Compendium-2.md']
SPECIAL = {'tower-2': ['python3', 'tower-2.py'], 'kinds': ['python3', 'kinds.py', 'The_Method_1_6___The_Register-2.md'],
           'minmax': ['python3', 'minmax.py'], 'r2-tools-constants': ['python3', 'r2-tools.py', 'constants'],
           'extent': ['python3', 'gate.py', 'extent-sites']}
CORE = ['tower-2', 'kinds', 'minmax', 'r2-tools-constants', 'extent']
MEMBER = re.compile(rb'^<<<FILE: (.+?)>>>\n(.*?)<<<END FILE: \1>>>\n', re.S | re.M)
md5 = lambda b: hashlib.md5(b).hexdigest()

def members_of(path):
    t = open(path, 'rb').read()
    ms = [(m.group(1).decode(), m.group(2)) for m in MEMBER.finditer(t)]
    assert len(set(n for n, _ in ms)) == len(ms), 'duplicate member name'
    return t, ms

def log(step, name, status, secs=''):
    with open(LOG, 'a', encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write(f'{step}\t{name}\t{status}\t{secs}\n')

def comp_path(argv):
    if '--comp' in argv: return argv[argv.index('--comp') + 1]
    c = sorted(f for f in os.listdir(HOME) if re.match(r'The_Method_1_6_BUILD\d+_compendia', f))
    assert len(c) == 1, f'name the compendia bundle with --comp (found {c})'
    return os.path.join(HOME, c[0])

def manifest(argv):
    main = argv[argv.index('--main') + 1] if '--main' in argv else MAIN
    comp = comp_path(argv)
    ok = True; rows = {}
    for tag, path in (('main', main), ('compendia', comp)):
        t, ms = members_of(path)
        print(f'{tag}: {os.path.basename(path)}  {len(t):,} B  md5 {md5(t)}  {t.count(b"\n"):,} lines  {len(ms)} members')
        for n, b in ms: rows[(tag, n)] = (len(b), md5(b), b.count(b'\n'), b)
    man = rows.get(('compendia', 'MANIFEST.tsv'))
    if man is None: print('FAIL: no MANIFEST.tsv member'); log('manifest', 'MANIFEST.tsv', 'FAIL'); return
    print(f'MANIFEST.tsv  {man[0]:,} B  md5 {man[1]}')
    listed = {}
    for line in man[3].decode('utf-8').splitlines()[1:]:
        tag, n, by, h, ln = line.split('\t'); listed[(tag, n)] = (int(by), h, int(ln))
    for key, (by, h, ln, _) in sorted(rows.items()):
        if key == ('compendia', 'MANIFEST.tsv'): continue
        if key not in listed: print('FAIL unlisted member', key); ok = False; continue
        if listed[key] != (by, h, ln): print('FAIL mismatch', key, 'bundle', (by, h, ln), 'manifest', listed[key]); ok = False
    for key in listed:
        if key not in rows: print('FAIL listed but absent', key); ok = False
    # extracted files
    ext = [f for f in os.listdir(H) if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(H, f))]
    for (tag, n), (by, h, ln, b) in rows.items():
        p = os.path.join(H, n)
        if not os.path.exists(p): print('FAIL not extracted', n); ok = False
        elif open(p, 'rb').read() != b: print('FAIL extracted file differs from bundle', n); ok = False
    extra = set(ext) - {n for _, n in rows}
    if extra: print('note: files in members/ not in any bundle:', sorted(extra))
    print(f'{"MANIFEST OK" if ok else "MANIFEST FAIL"}: {len(listed)} members listed, {len(ext)} files extracted')
    log('manifest', f'{md5(open(main,"rb").read())} {md5(open(comp,"rb").read())} {man[1]}', 'OK' if ok else 'FAIL')

def command(name):
    return SPECIAL.get(name, ['python3', name + '.py'])

def run_one(name, timeout=270):
    cmd = command(name); t0 = time.time()
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=H, capture_output=True, timeout=timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return 'TIMEOUT', '', time.time() - t0
    out = p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace'); err = p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    if p.returncode != 0: return 'ERROR', out + err, time.time() - t0
    return 'OK', out, time.time() - t0

def run(argv):
    names = CORE if '--core' in argv else (sorted(f[:-4] for f in os.listdir(H) if f.endswith('.out')) if '--all' in argv else argv)
    for name in names:
        gold = os.path.join(H, name + '.out')
        if not os.path.exists(gold): print(f'FAIL {name}: no {name}.out'); log('run', name, 'FAIL'); continue
        status, out, secs = run_one(name)
        if status == 'OK':
            g = open(gold, encoding='utf-8').read()
            if out == g: print(f'OK   {name}  ({secs:.0f} s)'); log('run', name, 'OK', f'{secs:.0f}'); continue
            d = list(difflib.unified_diff(g.splitlines(), out.splitlines(), 'banked', 'now', lineterm='', n=0))
            print(f'FAIL {name}: output differs from {name}.out ({len(d)} diff lines; first 40):'); print('\n'.join(d[:40]))
            log('run', name, 'FAIL', f'{secs:.0f}')
        else:
            print(f'FAIL {name}: {status}\n{out[-1500:]}'); log('run', name, status, f'{secs:.0f}')

def bank(argv):
    for name in argv:
        gold = os.path.join(H, name + '.out')
        assert not os.path.exists(gold), f'{gold} exists — never overwrite'
        status, out, secs = run_one(name)
        assert status == 'OK', f'{name}: {status}\n{out[-1500:]}'
        open(gold, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(out)
        print(f'banked {name}.out  {len(out.encode()):,} B  md5 {md5(out.encode())[:8]}  {out.count(chr(10))} lines  ({secs:.0f} s)')

def census():
    target = os.path.join(HOME, 'DEFECT-CENSUS.tsv')
    assert not os.path.exists(target), f'{target} exists — remove it in a delete-only call first'
    pc = os.path.join(H, '__pycache__'); assert not os.path.exists(pc), 'remove members/__pycache__ first (delete-only call)'
    status, out, secs = run_one('census')
    if status != 'OK': print(f'FAIL census: {status}\n{out[-1500:]}'); log('census', 'census.py', status); return
    same = open(target, 'rb').read() == open(os.path.join(H, 'DEFECT-CENSUS.tsv'), 'rb').read()
    print(f'{"OK  " if same else "FAIL"} census: DEFECT-CENSUS.tsv {"byte-identical to" if same else "DIFFERS from"} the member  ({secs:.0f} s)')
    log('census', 'DEFECT-CENSUS.tsv', 'OK' if same else 'FAIL', f'{secs:.0f}')

def extent_sites():
    reg = open(os.path.join(H, VOLS[1]), encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines()
    m = re.search(r'1 to (\d+)', reg[5]); assert m, 'Register L6 carries no "1 to N"'
    N = int(m.group(1)); print(f'extent from Register L6: 1 to {N}')
    for pat in (f'1 to {N}', f'1 to {N-1}'):
        sites = []
        for v in VOLS:
            for i, l in enumerate(open(os.path.join(H, v), encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines(), 1):
                if pat in l: sites.append(f'{v.split("___")[-1].replace("The_Method_1_6-2.md","main")}:L{i}')
        print(f'"{pat}": {len(sites)} sites', ' '.join(sites))

def cert(argv):
    chat = argv[0]
    rows = [l.rstrip('\n').split('\t') for l in open(LOG, encoding='utf-8')]
    steps = {(r[0], r[1]): r[2] for r in rows}
    need = [('manifest', None), ('census', 'DEFECT-CENSUS.tsv')] + [('run', n) for n in CORE]
    missing = [f'{s}:{n}' for s, n in need if not any(k[0] == s and (n is None or k[1] == n) for k in steps)]
    fails = [f'{k[0]}:{k[1]}={v}' for k, v in steps.items() if v != 'OK']
    verdict = 'PASS' if not missing and not fails else 'FAIL'
    lines = [f'GATE-ch{chat}  {time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC", time.gmtime())}  verdict {verdict}']
    lines += [f'  {r[0]:9} {r[1][:90]:90} {r[2]:8} {r[3]}' for r in rows]
    if missing: lines.append('  MISSING steps: ' + ' '.join(missing))
    if fails: lines.append('  FAILED steps: ' + ' '.join(fails))
    out = os.path.join(HOME, f'GATE-ch{chat}.txt'); assert not os.path.exists(out), f'{out} exists'
    open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n'); print('\n'.join(lines))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    step, rest = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:]
    {'manifest': manifest, 'run': run, 'bank': bank, 'census': lambda a: census(), 'extent-sites': lambda a: extent_sites(), 'cert': cert}[step](rest)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""close.py — the guarded build at a chat's close (chat 74, ruling 2).
  python3 members/close.py --old OLD_BUNDLE --new NEW_BUNDLE --w W-NNN.md [--main MAIN_BUNDLE] --members f1 f2 ...
Does, in order, and refuses on any failure: (1) asserts NEW does not exist and no new member name collides;
(2) appends the W-NNN text (must begin '### W-' and end '\\n\\n') to the WORKING-REGISTER.md body, immediately before its END marker;
(3) appends each member after the last END marker as '\\n<<<FILE: name>>>\\n' + body + '<<<END FILE: name>>>\\n' (body must end '\\n');
(4) computes MANIFEST.tsv over every member of the main bundle and of the new compendia bundle (except MANIFEST.tsv itself)
    and replaces the MANIFEST.tsv member body, or appends MANIFEST.tsv as a member if the old bundle had none;
(5) measures bytes / md5 / lines / members; (6) checks that among old members only WORKING-REGISTER.md and MANIFEST.tsv changed,
    and that the new WR body = old body + W text; (7) reverse guard: strips the appended members and the W text and restores the
    old MANIFEST body (or removes the MANIFEST member) and asserts the result's md5 equals the old bundle's; (8) writes NEW."""
import sys, os, re, hashlib
MEMBER = re.compile(rb'^<<<FILE: (.+?)>>>\n(.*?)<<<END FILE: \1>>>\n', re.S | re.M)
md5 = lambda b: hashlib.md5(b).hexdigest()
def arg(k, default=None):
    return sys.argv[sys.argv.index(k) + 1] if k in sys.argv else default
def block(name, body): return b'\n<<<FILE: ' + name.encode() + b'>>>\n' + body + b'<<<END FILE: ' + name.encode() + b'>>>\n'
def parse(t):
    ms = [(m.group(1).decode(), m.group(2)) for m in MEMBER.finditer(t)]
    assert len(set(n for n, _ in ms)) == len(ms), 'duplicate member name'; return ms
def manifest_text(main_members, comp_members):
    rows = ['bundle\tname\tbytes\tmd5\tlines']
    for tag, ms in (('main', main_members), ('compendia', comp_members)):
        for n, b in sorted(ms):
            if n == 'MANIFEST.tsv': continue
            rows.append(f'{tag}\t{n}\t{len(b)}\t{md5(b)}\t{b.count(b"\n")}')
    return ('\n'.join(rows) + '\n').encode('utf-8')

old_p, new_p, w_p = arg('--old'), arg('--new'), arg('--w')
main_p = arg('--main', '/home/claude/The_Method_1_6_BUILD90_main_and_register.md')
mem_ps = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--members') + 1:] if '--members' in sys.argv else []
assert old_p and new_p and w_p, 'need --old --new --w'
assert not os.path.exists(new_p), f'{new_p} exists — never overwrite'
old = open(old_p, 'rb').read(); old_ms = parse(old); old_names = [n for n, _ in old_ms]
main_ms = parse(open(main_p, 'rb').read())
W = open(w_p, 'rb').read(); assert W.startswith(b'### W-') and W.endswith(b'\n\n'), 'W text must begin "### W-" and end with a blank line'
new_members = []
for p in mem_ps:
    n = os.path.basename(p); b = open(p, 'rb').read()
    assert n not in old_names and n not in [x for x, _ in new_members], f'member name collision: {n}'
    assert b.endswith(b'\n'), f'{n}: body must end with a newline'; new_members.append((n, b))
# (2) W text into the WR body
end = b'<<<END FILE: WORKING-REGISTER.md>>>\n'; assert old.count(end) == 1
i = old.index(end); assert old[i - 2:i] == b'\n\n', 'WR body must end with a blank line'
new = old[:i] + W + old[i:]
# (3) append members after the last END marker
assert new.endswith(b'>>>\n'), 'bundle must end with an END marker'
for n, b in new_members: new += block(n, b)
# (4) manifest
had_manifest = 'MANIFEST.tsv' in old_names
man_old = dict(old_ms).get('MANIFEST.tsv')
comp_ms = parse(new); man = manifest_text(main_ms, comp_ms)
if had_manifest:
    ob = b'<<<FILE: MANIFEST.tsv>>>\n' + man_old + b'<<<END FILE: MANIFEST.tsv>>>\n'; assert new.count(ob) == 1
    new = new.replace(ob, b'<<<FILE: MANIFEST.tsv>>>\n' + man + b'<<<END FILE: MANIFEST.tsv>>>\n')
else:
    new += block('MANIFEST.tsv', man)
# (5) measure
new_ms = parse(new); nd = dict(new_ms); od = dict(old_ms)
print(f'old {os.path.basename(old_p)}  {len(old):,} B  md5 {md5(old)}  {old.count(b"\n"):,} lines  {len(old_ms)} members')
print(f'new {os.path.basename(new_p)}  {len(new):,} B  md5 {md5(new)}  {new.count(b"\n"):,} lines  {len(new_ms)} members')
print(f'MANIFEST.tsv  {len(man):,} B  md5 {md5(man)}  {man.count(b"\n")} lines;  WORKING-REGISTER.md  {len(nd["WORKING-REGISTER.md"]):,} B  md5 {md5(nd["WORKING-REGISTER.md"])}  {nd["WORKING-REGISTER.md"].count(b"\n"):,} lines')
# (6) change set
changed = [n for n in old_names if nd[n] != od[n]]
assert set(changed) <= {'WORKING-REGISTER.md', 'MANIFEST.tsv'}, f'unexpected change in old members: {changed}'
assert nd['WORKING-REGISTER.md'] == od['WORKING-REGISTER.md'] + W, 'WR is not old + W'
added = [n for n, _ in new_ms if n not in od]
print(f'changed old members: {changed};  added members: {added};  lines +{new.count(b"\n") - old.count(b"\n")} / -0')
# (7) reverse guard
rev = new
for n, b in new_members: assert rev.count(block(n, b)) == 1; rev = rev.replace(block(n, b), b'')
if had_manifest:
    nb = b'<<<FILE: MANIFEST.tsv>>>\n' + man + b'<<<END FILE: MANIFEST.tsv>>>\n'; assert rev.count(nb) == 1
    rev = rev.replace(nb, b'<<<FILE: MANIFEST.tsv>>>\n' + man_old + b'<<<END FILE: MANIFEST.tsv>>>\n')
else:
    assert rev.count(block('MANIFEST.tsv', man)) == 1; rev = rev.replace(block('MANIFEST.tsv', man), b'')
assert rev.count(W + end) == 1; rev = rev.replace(W + end, end)
print(f'reverse recovers md5 {md5(rev)}  == old: {md5(rev) == md5(old)}')
assert md5(rev) == md5(old), 'REVERSE GUARD FAILED — nothing written'
# (8) write
open(new_p, 'wb').write(new); print('written', new_p)

input.command:
cd /home/claude && timeout 280 python3 - <<'EOF'
import hashlib
L=open('HANDOFF-25.md',encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
rul=L[3]; assert rul.startswith('- **Rulings in force**'); rul=rul[2:]
dfr=L[35]; assert dfr.startswith("All of HANDOFF-24's list stands")
R='''# RULINGS-R2.md — rulings and standing discipline in force during Phase R2 (append-only)

This member replaces the rulings paragraph of the handoff (chat 74, ruling 3). A chat appends a dated block when M rules; nothing here is edited or removed. The Register is a different object (subject matter only); this is process.

## As restated in HANDOFF-25 (chat 74), verbatim

'''+rul+'''

## Chat 74 (30 August 2026) — session-throughput rulings

1. **Declined:** direct upload of the bundles as an archive (M: not enough internal storage). The gate keeps fetching both bundles from Drive by title; Drive remains the store.
2. **Approved:** the gate and the close as instruments — gate.py (MANIFEST.tsv verification of both bundles, golden-output runs printing only mismatches, census, extent sites, certificate), close.py (guarded build with manifest and reverse recovery), r2lib.py (shared functions lifted verbatim from the instruments), banked NAME.out goldens for every deterministic instrument. Instrument design remains Claude's.
3. **Approved:** the handoff carries identity (chat, build, Register range, md5s), the bootstrap, the gate run list, next work, Drive actions and the prompt; rulings live here and deferred items in DEFERRED.md, both append-only.
4. **Approved:** built in chat 74 itself (BUILD101 + HANDOFF-26; HANDOFF-25 and BUILD100 retired unused).

Measured basis (chat 74 transcript, byte shares): gate 32 %, close 10 %, reading 57 %; each Drive fetch leaves a ~65 KB base64 preview in context (13 % of the chat for the two). Rulings 2–4 remove the by-eye comparison and the handoff growth; ruling 1 leaves the fetch cost as it is.
'''
D='''# DEFERRED.md — cross-chapter items deferred during Phase R2 (append-only)

Do not re-derive; settle each item in the chapter named. An item is closed by a later line that cites the READ file closing it — never by deletion. This member replaces the deferred paragraph of the handoff (chat 74, ruling 3).

## As of HANDOFF-25 (chat 74), verbatim

'''+dfr+'''

## Chat 74 additions (instruments)

- r2lib.py lifts, verbatim by AST, the functions of r2-ch12f (build9, src, tgt, leq, tarjan, analyse), r2-ch12d (is_tree), r2-ch12i (closure, factor_q, ci, components, separates), r2-ch12j (support, direct, composed) and r2-ch12k (mi, ci_sets — parameterised). The functions of r2-ch12c (closure/leq/jn/mt/E_np), r2-ch12e (comp/sep/cyc), r2-ch12g (encode/closed/pairs) and r2-ch12h (reach/price) are not yet lifted: lift them into r2lib when a segment next needs them, verbatim, with provenance comments.
- r2-ch12c.py is not banked as a golden (it prints wall-clock time); its figures stand as recorded in W-108 and READ-ch12c.md. All other instruments of chats 71–74 are banked (fifteen NAME.out members) and reproduce deterministically.
'''
for name,txt in (('RULINGS-R2.md',R),('DEFERRED.md',D)):
    b=txt.encode('utf-8'); open('members/'+name,'wb').write(b); print(name, len(b),'B', hashlib.md5(b).hexdigest()[:8], b.count(b'\n'),'lines')
EOF

### W-111 — THE GATE AND THE CLOSE AS INSTRUMENTS; r2lib; RULINGS AND DEFERRED ITEMS AS MEMBERS (chat 74, second segment; BUILD101 compendia)

*Occasion.* After BUILD100 and HANDOFF-25 were delivered, M asked whether the sessions could get more done, the gate taking too long to clear. MEASURED from chat 74's transcript (byte shares of the whole chat): gate 32 %, close 10 %, the three reading segments 57 % (25.7 / 17.3 / 13.6). Inside the gate the two Drive fetches were the largest single item — each left a base64 preview of ~65 KB in context (65,351 and 65,345 characters), 13 % of the chat, unused, since both bundles are decoded from the spilled files; the remainder was the by-eye comparison of ~60 member md5s and ~150 lines of instrument output against a handoff of 22 KB growing ~2.5 KB a chat (INFERRED for the by-eye share). M ruled: 1 declined (no archive upload — not enough internal storage; the gate keeps fetching from Drive); 2, 3, 4 approved (instruments; slim handoff with rulings and deferred items as append-only members; built in this chat). Rulings recorded in RULINGS-R2.md.

*Built (all in members/, all new members of BUILD101).* **r2lib.py** (11,146 B): load_tower, read_member, md5, lam9p, gG_index, the Λ₉/Λ₉′ and (g, G) constants, and functions lifted VERBATIM by AST source segment from r2-ch12f (build9, src, tgt, leq, tarjan, analyse), r2-ch12d (is_tree), r2-ch12i (closure, factor_q, ci, components, separates), r2-ch12j (support, direct, composed), r2-ch12k (mi with N = len(xs), ci_sets with X as first argument — the only two edits, count-asserted); smoke test MEASURED: |Λ₉| 1,654, |Λ₉′| 1,561, is_tree True/False, closure (2,436,721, 0, 0), ci f ⊥ 2S′ | g (16, 0, 0) / (16, 6, 1), direct {0: 1, 1: 3} vs composed {0: 2, 1: 3}, |(g, G)| 13,775, I(ℓ;k) 0.353, ci_sets (2,442, 0), build9 1,654. **gate.py**: `manifest` (every member of both bundles against MANIFEST.tsv — bytes, md5, lines — and every extracted file against the bundle text), `run NAME… | --core | --all` (each NAME.out golden is diffed against the instrument's stdout; only mismatches print), `census` (refuses if a scratch DEFECT-CENSUS.tsv or a pycache exists; byte compare), `extent-sites` (reads N from Register L6, prints the "1 to N" and "1 to N−1" sites of the six volumes), `bank` (writes NAME.out, never overwrites), `cert CHAT` (PASS only if manifest, census and the five core runs are logged OK and nothing failed). **close.py**: refuses an existing target or a name collision; appends the W text (must begin "### W-", end with a blank line) before the WR END marker; appends members after the last END marker; writes MANIFEST.tsv (bundle, name, bytes, md5, lines over both bundles, excluding itself; replaced if present, appended if not); asserts only WORKING-REGISTER.md and MANIFEST.tsv changed among old members and that the WR = old + W; reverse-recovers the old bundle's md5 before writing. **RULINGS-R2.md** and **DEFERRED.md**: HANDOFF-25's rulings and deferred paragraphs verbatim plus this chat's blocks; append-only. **Fifteen goldens**: tower-2, kinds, minmax, r2-tools-constants, extent, r2-ch12a/b/d/e/f/g/h/i/j/k (.out); r2-ch12c excluded (prints wall-clock time).

*Tests (MEASURED).* `gate.py run --all`: 15 of 15 OK in 52 s and 15 lines of output. Failure test: a scratch instrument banked, changed, rerun → FAIL with the unified diff; an unbanked name → FAIL; scratch and test log then deleted in a delete-only call. `gate.py census` OK (byte-identical, 13 s) after the scratch DEFECT-CENSUS.tsv and members/__pycache__ were removed; `run --core` 5 of 5 OK. close.py's guards: collision, missing trailing newline, W text form, unexpected change in an old member, reverse mismatch — each an assertion before anything is written.

*Close.* BUILD101 = BUILD100 (md5 43524357… ← 4204a2dbec32ef9754df49eacaf73946 is BUILD100's md5, which the reverse guard must recover) + this entry + twenty members (r2lib.py, gate.py, close.py, RULINGS-R2.md, DEFERRED.md, fifteen .out) + MANIFEST.tsv. No volume changed; no Register entry; no correction. HANDOFF-26 in the slim form supersedes HANDOFF-25 (retired unused, with BUILD100). Next: Phase R2 at main §12.11.0.8 (L2842–2897); expected effect (INFERRED): gate ≈ 12 % of a chat with the fetch previews, close ≈ 5 %, four to five reading segments a chat.
